items.w: אברכה את יהוה בכל עת תמיד תהלתו בפי
items.title: CONTINUING GRATITUDE
items.quote: I will bless Hashem at all times; His praise will always be in my mouth.
items.text: There should never be a time when you are not grateful to Him. You should feel that everything that you experience is miraculous.

items.title: THE SOURCE
items.quote: My soul takes pride in Hashem.
items.text: Recognize that everything good that happens to you is from Hashem, the Source of all good. Take nothing for granted.

items.title: THE HUMBLE
items.quote: Let the humble people hear and be glad.
items.text: Share your feeling of joy and gratitude with those who are capable of suppressing their own pride to acknowledge their debt to Hashem.

items.w: גדלו ליהוה אתי ונרוממה שמו יחדו
items.title: GREATNESS
items.quote: Declare the greatness of Hashem with me. Together let us recognize His Name as sublime.
items.text: The greatness of Hashem can best be recognized in a group of like-minded people who inspire each other with their enthusiasm.

items.w: דרשתי את יהוה וענני ומכל מגורותי הצילני
items.title: SEEKING
items.quote: I sought Hashem and He answered. He rescued me from all my terrors.
items.text: When you have a need of Hashem’s help, your primary focus should not be on your request but upon your relationship with Hashem. You should seek to be closer to Him and the solution to your problems will inevitably result.

items.w: הביטו אליו ונהרו ופניהם אל יחפרו
items.title: SEEING THE LIGHT
items.quote: Others have looked to Him and received light. Their faces were not shamed.
items.text: Don’t be discouraged at not feeling the closeness of Hashem. Just as others have looked to Hashem and were granted access to His light, so will you. You will not be disappointed if you are sincere.

items.title: POVERTY
items.quote: This poor man [David] called and Hashem heard.
items.text: No matter how successful you have been in life or how strong you are, when you approach Hashem think of yourself as abjectly poor. Everything you have is His. Without Him you have nothing and therefore you are totally dependent upon Him.

items.w: זה עני קרא ויהוה שמע ומכל צרותיו הושיעו
items.quote: This poor man [David] called and Hashem heard. And from all his troubles He saved him.

items.title: FEAR
items.quote: The angel of Hashem encamps [protectively] around those who fear Him.
items.text: As long as you fear only Hashem, He will see that you are protected. There is no reason to fear an attacker for he has no power to harm you unless it is the will of Hashem.

items.title: REALITY
items.quote: Examine and see that Hashem is good.
items.text: Examine your experiences of life honestly and you will realize how good Hashem has been to you.

items.quote: Fortunate is the man [of might] who takes refuge in Him.
items.text: He knows this might belongs to Hashem.

items.w: יראו את יהוה קדשיו כי אין מחסור ליראיו
items.title: DEPRIVATION
items.quote: Fear Hashem, [you,] His holy ones. for there is no deprivation to those who fear Him.
items.text: Don’t be discouraged from living a holy life, for you will not suffer from deprivation.

items.w: כפירים רשו ורעבו ודרשי יהוה לא יחסרו כל טוב
items.quote: Young lions are in want and hunger, but those who seek Hashem will not lack any good.

items.title: COMING AND GOING
items.quote: Come, children, listen to me.
items.text: To achieve a change in attitude you must go as well as come. You must go away from your defective thinking by recognizing its fallacies; then you will be open to new and better ideas.

items.quote: I will teach you the fear of Hashem.
items.text: The fear of Hashem does not come to a person without effort. He must exert himself to give up his old attitude and learn a new attitude.

items.title: LIFE
items.quote: Who is the man who wants life?
items.text: Everybody wants life but not everybody is willing to sacrifice his momentary desires to achieve the physical and spiritual health that are essential to long life in this world and the next.

items.title: DAYS
items.quote: cherishes days.
items.text: You should aspire to cherish every day of your life, to utilize it to its full potential.

items.title: GOOD
items.quote: seeing good.
items.text: You should aspire to cherish that which has true value in life, as opposed to material wealth that has only superficial value.

items.w: נצר לשונך מרע ושפתיך מדבר מרמה
items.title: ON GUARD
items.quote: Guard your tongue from evil, your lips from speaking deceit.
items.text: Your tongue and lips may be inclined to utter inappropriate words unthinkingly, as though they are acting independently of you. Your challenge is to control them and restrain them.

items.title: THE WRONG ROAD
items.quote: Turn away from evil and do good.
items.text: Don’t assume that as long as you are not choosing an evil road, you are doing good. You may already be on the wrong road and evil is waiting for you somewhere along the way, unless you stop and examine your life.

items.title: PEACE
items.quote: Seek peace and pursue it.
items.text: It is not sufficient to avoid starting a dispute. You need to put your energy into identifying any situation which has the potential for dispute or where ill will among people already exists. Once you have identified such a situation you need to actively pursue strategies to overcome it.

items.title: EYES
items.quote: The eyes of Hashem are toward the righteous.
items.text: Hashem sees everything in the universe, but His purpose in creating the world is fulfilled by what He sees in the the righteous.

items.title: EYES
items.quote: The eyes of Hashem are toward the righteous.
items.text: Hashem sees everything in the universe, but His purpose in creating the world is fulfilled by what He sees in the the righteous.

items.w: צעקו ויהוה שמע ומכל צרותם הצילם
items.title: HATZALAH AND YESHUAH
items.quote: If they have cried out, He rescues them from all their troubles.
items.text: Hashem rescues the wicked who have cried out, but he reserves a yeshuah (salvation) for the humble tzadik, as it says in posuk 7, “And from all his troubles He saved him.” The difference is that yeshuah implies forming a bond or bris with the person being saved, whereas rescue (hatzalah) refers only to the act of recovery from distress.
